name: jsonl
algorithm: Read an NDJSON event log line by line through a 64 KiB buffered reader, decode each line into a typed record with the language's JSON library, group the ok events by user (count, sums, minimum and maximum, tag and message lengths), sort the groups, and write the report as one compact JSON object with the library's serialiser (README.md).

rust.name: serde
rust.inside: serde_core 1.0.229 and the serde_derive 1.0.229 procedural macro (built on syn 3.0.9, quote 1.0.47, proc-macro2 1.0.107 and unicode-ident 1.0.27, which run at compile time only); a few unsafe blocks

rust.name: serde_json
rust.inside: unsafe Rust in its reader and writer; itoa 1.0.18 and zmij 1.0.21 (unsafe Rust) for number text; its own word-at-a-time string scan (unsafe pointer arithmetic); memchr 2.8.0 (unsafe Rust and SIMD), linked for raw byte strings and error positions, which this row does not reach

skip.c: no std JSON in C, and no C JSON library is vendored

notes: The checksum is the SHA-256 of the whole report: its strings are user names of ASCII letters and digits and its numbers are integers, so every library writes the same bytes (no <, > or & to escape, no float spelling).

Each language uses its default hash map and hash: Mk Map.New and Zig StringHashMap are fixed, Rust HashMap (SipHash-1-3, per RandomState) and Go's map (per map) are seeded at run time (README.md, Cells).

Mk's FromJson goes through json.Parse's Value and copies every string into the line arena (D-461); Zig's parseFromSliceLeaky leaves a string with no escape as a view of the line; Go and Rust allocate each string. Each is its library's own way.
